Order 
This is first bail application filed on behalf of applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

2. The applicant is in jail since 24.09.2025 in connection with Crime No.84 of 2025 registered at P.S. Bahoriband Thana, District - Katni for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 34 of the IPC.

3. Prosecution story in brief is that applicant as well as co-accused persons colluded together and thereafter executed an agreement of sale with respect to Survey No.1149, whereas, co-accused Sheetal was not owner of Survey No.1149 and present applicant signed aforesaid agreement of sale as attesting witness.
Further, applicant executed an agreement of sale with complainant with respect to Survey No.1150 but later-on, sold the property to someone else.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63306 2 MCRC-46905-2025 4.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that present applicant executed agreement of sale on 26.02.2024 with complainant with respect to Survey No.1150 for an amount of Rs.14,35,000/-.

1 the time of execution of agreement of sale, applicant received Rs.5,00,000/- and remaining amount was to be paid within two months from the date of execution of agreement of sale.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that within the stipulated period as mentioned in agreement of sale, complainant did not pay the remaining amount.
Therefore, applicant sold the property to someone on 16.05.2024.
It is also urged that applicant has paid Rs.2,00,000/- to complainant in police station.
He is ready to refund the remaining amount of Rs.3,00,000/- to complainant.
It is also urged that present applicant is in nowhere connected with the Survey No.1149 and he has only signed agreement of sale with respect to Survey No.1149 as attesting witness.
No custodial interrogation is required.
Applicant is in jail since 24.09.2025.
On above grounds, it is urged that applicant be released on bail.

5. Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State as well as learned counsel for the objector have opposed the application and submits that applicant and co-accused Sheetal colluded together and thereafter executed an agreement to sale with respect to Survey No.1149, whereas, co-accused Sheetal was not owner of the property.
Owner of the property was one Indri Bai .
Applicant has signed aforesaid documents as attesting witness.
It is also urged that both applicant and co-accused have received the sale consideration of both Survey No.1149 and Survey No.1150 jointly.

Admittedly,
Sheetal is not owner of Survey No.1149.
Therefore, applicant is not entitled to be NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63306 3 MCRC-46905-2025 released on bail.
6. This Court has examined submissions of learned counsel for the parties in the light of evidence available and record.
7. Having regard to nature of dispute between the parties and also the fact that applicant is ready to deposit an amount of Rs.3,00,000/-., I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.

8. It is directed that subject to deposit Rs.3,00,000/- before trial Court, applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
9. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
10. Soft copy of this bail order be sent immediately/forthwith to the applicant through concerned Jail Superintendent.
11. M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
